How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was a bit confusing knowing where to find the right information. I was very much in doubt about which courses I was allowed to take. I wanted to take courses in Norwegian, but they where not listed in the document of courses for exchange students. But I found out that I could sign up for them anyway. It would be helpful to have more clear information about which courses are available.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I did email the exchange coordinator at UiT and a got a reply every time, but it was nok always clear

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: i managed to registrate for all the classes i wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: For the first application and the application you can apply for more that 30 ECTS and change it later. I highly recommend that.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I was pretty prepared that it it expensive to live in Norway, but most prices are comparable with Denmark.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
All "tourist activities" like whale- or northern light safari, sleigh riding with reindeer etc is very expensive. 
Going out in Norway is expensive, so it is good to know that many bars give student discount. And also some shops, like interior shop "princess".
You can borrow skies for free at BUA.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are so many opportunities for skiing, hiking, and cultural activities like museums and loads of festivals etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
For sure go skiing, either cross country or in the alpin park. You can borrow skies for free at BUA. 
I volunteered ad both TIFF (Tromsø international Film Festival) and performing arts festival Vårscenefest. I really recommend that as it is a great way to meet people and get free tickets and great experiences. 
I also went on a trip to Lofoten with the ferry, which was very beautiful.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Skiing or hiking in the surrounding areas, a trip to Sommarøy, Senja or Lofoten.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy. It takes some time to get used to the language, but as danes we can understand each other, and we dont need to speak english.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The eager to go out and experience nature.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Experience some of the festivals the city has to offer, like Tromsø international Film Festival, Silent film festival, Vårscenefest, Nordlysfestivalen, Insomnia, etc. 
You will learn to understand norwegian fast, just practice.
Experience nature!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot of bars and some shops have student discount.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All in all a very positive and rewarding experience.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Getting used to a new school, finding my way around, learning the online portal etc.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
